groeit.title: The neighbourhood grows
groeit.lead: The same area in four years. On the right the Boerenwetering, bottom left the Roelof Hartplein.
groeit.caption: Schematic, not to scale: the positions of houses and factory are approximate.

jaren.tekst: Scattered wooden houses. One bridge, at the Ruysdaelstraat. The factory next door.
More houses on the sand. The factory is demolished; the Hobbemakade can be built.
Closed housing blocks, the Roelof Hartplein is finished. A second bridge at the Roelof Hartstraat.
Neighbourhood KD09 in the Museum Quarter: about 60,000 m² between five streets.

eilanden.title: Two islands, one timeline
eilanden.lead: Dreyfus's Devil's Island and Amsterdam's Devil's Island lasted just as long — and both ended in 1906.
eilanden.desc: Two timelines from 1894 to 1906. Dreyfus: 1894 convicted, 1895 exiled to Devil's Island, 1899 pardoned, 1906 exonerated. Amsterdam: 1894 secondary school opens, 1896 annexation, 1896 to 1906 the nickname Duivelseiland, 1906 factory demolished.
eilanden.bijnaam: nickname "Devil's Island": remote, one bridge, the factory's stench

fabriek.title: The factory in numbers
fabriek.bedragTekst: is what the factory asked for its land. Too much, the city thought.

feiten.tekst: The land becomes part of Amsterdam; the factory stays.
No villas around it, but a circus, a cycling school and a fire station.
The city buys the factory and demolishes it. (Another source says 1910.)
A second way in along the Boerenwetering: the Hobbemakade.

fabriek.desc: Cross-section from north to south: the factory with its chimney, the Ruysdaelstraat and the houses of Duivelseiland. A cloud of stench drifts from the chimney over the houses; waste water flows into the Boerenwetering.
fabriek.caption: Schematic cross-section, not to scale.

omDeHoek.title: Along the Hobbemakade, around 1900

omDeHoek.desc: Along the Hobbemakade from north to south: 1 teacher training school, the Hobbemastraat, 2 Velox cycling school, 3 fire station, the Honthorststraat, 4 Circus Arena, the candle factory, the Ruysdaelstraat and then Duivelseiland.

hero.intro: Rubbish next to containers and sofas on the pavement are a major source of irritation in the neighbourhood. Here you can read how it works, where things go and where it often goes wrong. All figures come live from the City of Amsterdam's open data.

geluid.heading: Noise
geluid.metaDescription: Renovations, DIY and parties in Duivelseiland: when noise is allowed, how to let the neighbours know and what to do about noise nuisance. With an instruction card and notes for the neighbours.

hero.lead: People in this neighbourhood live close together. The inner courtyards act like sound boxes, and it is appreciated when you keep that in mind.
body: Hold off on noisy tools like drills and sanders until a little later in the day, and don’t ask the builders to start with them at 7 am.
Let your neighbours know as soon as a renovation is coming and how long it will take. Many people work from home, so they can plan around it.

kern.text: Companies may build and demolish Monday to Saturday
and public holidays: no construction noise, not even from a contractor
No permit needed. Do tell the neighbours in advance
An outdoor street party may last until then, with a notification 2 weeks ahead

verbouwen.name: Renovating and DIY
verbouwen.message: Contractors have fixed hours. If you do the work yourself, there are no fixed hours, but you must avoid unnecessary noise.
verbouwen.factText: Monday to Saturday, for construction and demolition by a company

feestjes.name: Parties
feestjes.message: A party at home is fine. The city only steps in when serious nuisance keeps happening.
feestjes.factText: permits needed for a party at home or in the garden

overlast.name: Bothered by noise?
overlast.message: Start with a conversation. If you can’t sort it out together, there are free mediators and a hotline that is open day and night.
overlast.factText: open: the city’s neighbour nuisance hotline, 020 552 5000

vooraf.name: Knowing what’s coming
vooraf.message: A renovation next door doesn’t have to be a surprise.
vooraf.factText: before work starts, the building sign must be up, for renovations with a permit

verbouwen.weekSub: Construction and demolition by a contractor or handyman company. For DIY, this is the best guideline.

week.label: Week from Monday to Sunday, from midnight to midnight
week.summary: Monday to Saturday from {van} to {tot} it is allowed. Preferably no drilling or sanding before {advies}. No construction noise on Sundays and public holidays.
week.advies: Allowed, but preferably no drilling or sanding yet
week.feestdag: Public holidays count as Sundays: New Year’s Day, Easter Monday, Whit Monday, Ascension Day, King’s Day, 5 May and both Christmas days. Good Friday counts too.

advies.title: The law allows 7 am, but…
advies.text: The courtyards echo, and many neighbours work from home or are still asleep. Start noisy work such as drilling, grinding, sanding and breaking a little later in the day, and agree on this with the contractor. Builders who start at 7 can do quiet work first.

grenzen.title: How loud may it be?
grenzen.sub: The louder the noise at the front of a home, the fewer days it is allowed, per building project.
head: Noise at the facade
Maximum
grenzen.note: In dB(A). For comparison: a conversation is about 60 dB, a drill up close 90 to 100 dB.

klussen.title: Doing it yourself
text: If you do the work yourself, the law sets no fixed hours. You do have a duty of care: you must avoid unnecessary noise.
So keep to the same hours as a contractor, and do the noisiest work in the middle of the day. The city also mentions Monday to Saturday, {van} to {tot}.
Also check your owners’ association (VvE) rules or your rental contract: they sometimes have stricter rules.

buren.title: Telling the neighbours
buren.text: Ring the bell or drop a note through the letterbox: when does it start, how long will it take, and when will it be noisy? Neighbours who work from home can then plan around it.
buren.bouwbord: Do you need an environmental permit? Then a building sign must be up at least a week before work starts, at least A3 size, saying how long the work will take and who to contact. You can pick up a free sign at a city office (stadsloket).
buren.briefjeCta: Make a note for the neighbours
buren.gemeenteCta: Examples and building sign from the city (Dutch)

ontheffing.title: Working in the evening, at night or on Sunday
ontheffing.text: For that, the company needs a noise exemption from the city (officially a ‘maatwerkvoorschrift’). It is only granted if:
items: the work is really necessary and can’t be done during the day (catching up on a schedule doesn’t count);
the quietest methods and machines are used;
the application is in at least {weken} weeks ahead.
ontheffing.kosten: An exemption costs {bedrag} per night. Whoever has one must give the neighbours a letter a week in advance with a phone number for complaints.
ontheffing.cta: Construction noise exemption at the city (Dutch)

thuis.title: A party at home or in the garden
text: You don’t need a permit, and there is no fixed time by which it must be quiet.

The rule is that you don’t cause your neighbours serious nuisance that keeps coming back, for example so that they often can’t sleep. Some noise comes with living close together. The city itself gives the example that a barbecue in the shared garden a few times a year is no reason to step in.

tips.title: Keeping it fun for everyone
items: Tell the neighbours in advance: when, until what time, and a phone number.
After 11 pm, turn the music down and close the windows and doors.
Talking and laughing on a balcony or in the courtyard carries far: keep it quiet there in the evening.
Invite the neighbours. People who can join in are less bothered.
tips.briefjeCta: Make a party note for the neighbours

buiten.title: Outdoor street party
buiten.intro: In the street or on a square, a free notification at least {weken} weeks ahead is enough, if the party meets these conditions:
items: at most {max} visitors at the same time;
no louder than {db} dB(C) at the facades of the surrounding homes;
not on the road and not blocking traffic;
no sale of food or drink, not commercial;
at most two small objects, such as a party tent;
there is an organiser who can be approached.
buiten.zondag: On Sundays, an exemption is needed before 1 pm. If the party doesn’t meet the conditions, it needs an event permit.
buiten.cta: Notify an event at the city (Dutch)

praten.title: Talk to your neighbours
praten.text: At a calm moment, not in the middle of the noise. Neighbours often don’t know it bothers you.

verhuurder.title: Renting? Go to the landlord. Own your home? The owners’ association (VvE)
verhuurder.text: They can hold the neighbours to the rental contract or the rules.

beterBuren.title: Ask for a neighbourhood mediator
beterBuren.text: BeterBuren helps neighbours sort things out together, free and confidential.

meldpunt.title: Report it to the neighbour nuisance hotline
meldpunt.text: The Meldpunt Zorg en Woonoverlast handles nuisance from a neighbour, including noise. Urgent reports are picked up right away, others within 2 working days.

bouw.title: Construction noise outside the hours?
bouw.text: Or do you suspect building without a permit? Report it to the city.

horeca.title: Bothered by a café or business?
horeca.text: The city has a separate way to report that.

logboek.title: Keep a record
logboek.text: Write down when and how long you were bothered, and what you heard. That helps the landlord, the mediator or the hotline, and is needed if it ever ends up in court.

nood.title: Is it unsafe?
nood.text: Call the police on <politieLink>{politie}</politieLink>. In an emergency: <noodLink>{nood}</noodLink>.

overlast.horecaCta: Report nuisance from bars and businesses (Dutch)

omgevingsalert.title: Permits in the neighbourhood
omgevingsalert.text: The Omgevingsalert app or Overheid.nl shows which building permits are applied for nearby. If you disagree, you can object.

nulmeting.title: Get a pre-construction survey
nulmeting.text: Are the neighbours doing a big renovation? Ask the contractor to record the state of your home beforehand, including the foundations. If the contractor won’t, you can hire a building inspector yourself.

schade.title: Damage from the renovation?
schade.text: For example cracks or water damage: first contact whoever is renovating. If you can’t work it out, the Juridisch Loket (free legal advice) can help.

sources.title: Sources
sources.intro: The rules on this page come from the City of Amsterdam and the law. We have summarised them in plain language.
sources.disclaimer: This is not legal advice. When in doubt, the city’s rules take precedence.

intro.title: Neighbourhood drinks
intro.lead: What began last winter with fire baskets and mulled wine in the snow became a lively afternoon in the sun on Sunday 6 September, on that same green. A huge turnout for neighbourhood drinks, and such a good time!
intro.doel: The idea is to do this more often. Not just for the party, but mainly to get to know each other: the neighbours three doors down, across the street, around the square. And to give that some continuity.

pincode.title: You need a PIN code
pincode.text: The AED cabinet opens with a PIN code. You receive it when you are called out via 112 as a HartslagNu citizen responder during a cardiac arrest. The code is then shown in the HartslagNu app or in the text or alert message.

noodgeval.title: Not a citizen responder?
noodgeval.text: In a real emergency, call 112 first. The dispatcher will give you instructions. Some AED cabinets can be opened remotely, or via the phone number on the cabinet.

inDeBuurt.title: Local amenities
inDeBuurt.intro: Places in and around Duivelseiland worth knowing about.

kerk.tekst: Sunday service, open church on Saturday afternoons, a drop-in coffee morning and rooms for hire. See their website for times and activities.

bibliotheek.tekst: The oldest branch of the Amsterdam Public Library still in use, in a listed building. Borrow books, a large children’s section, study spaces, computers and a reading café.

lydia.tekst: Community centre in the listed Huize Lydia building, run by volunteers together with Combiwel. Courses, workshops, sports and meetings for young and old, and rooms for hire.

parkeren.title: Parking in Duivelseiland
parkeren.intro: Duivelseiland is in parking permit area Zuid 8. Across the Hobbemakade, De Pijp begins: a residents’ permit for Zuid 8 is not valid there.

bezoeker.betalen: Pay: {tijden}. Outside those hours parking is free.
bezoeker.kaarten: Staying longer? At the parking meter you can buy a day ticket (Mon–Sat 9:00–24:00) for {dag}, a Sunday ticket (12:00–24:00) for {zondag} or an evening ticket (19:00–24:00) for {avond}.

bezoek.tekst: With the resident’s visitor permit, your visitors park at a 65 percent discount. The resident registers the visit, or the visitor can arrange it themselves, up to 150 hours per quarter. The permit is free, even if you don’t have a parking permit yourself.

bewoner.tekst: With a parking permit for Zuid 8 you park in the neighbourhood without paying parking fees. The permit itself costs money and there may be a waiting list. It is not valid in De Pijp.

aanmelden.metaDescription: Submit an idea for a neighbourhood activity on Duivelseiland.
aanmelden.intro: Fancy starting a book club, cooking club or walking group? Submit your idea. We put it online so neighbours can join.
stappen: Submit your idea below. Nothing needs to exist yet: the idea is enough.
Within a week the editors check whether the idea fits the ground rules.
Once approved, it gets its own page. Neighbours sign up there and you're the organiser: you see who's joining, message the group and decide whether and when it goes ahead.
aanmelden.regelsIntro: An activity is meant to connect neighbours. That's why it must be:
regels: accessible: anyone can join, no experience or membership needed;
non-commercial: free, or just sharing costs (e.g. ingredients), with no profit;
inclusive: open to all residents, regardless of age, background or language;
held in or around the neighbourhood.
aanmelden.nietToegestaan: Not allowed: selling or promotion, recruiting for a business, political or religious recruitment, and closed groups.
